title: Session 1 — Participant 13 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Import and logistics reports — turn a warehouse/shipping Excel workbook into a set of interactive visual reports (warehouse stock, landed containers, in-transit shipment, upcoming orders, and a consolidated overview) with Claude's help.

Step 1.step_action: Create a visual image showing inventory stock by item and current inventory value.

nodes.label: Define the reporting objective and submit the warehouse data
nodes.detail: Uploads the 'Landed cost and allocation' Excel workbook to a new Claude desktop chat and asks for a report showing every warehouse item with all of its info displayed.

nodes.label: Extract warehouse data and generate an initial tabular report
nodes.detail: Reads and validates the warehouse sheet's 35 line items, builds a full landscape Word table report with every column plus a totals row, catches and fixes a page-dimension bug so the table fits the page, and delivers the finished document.

nodes.label: Review the initial report and request a more visual redesign
nodes.detail: Judges the plain table report insufficient and asks for something more visually attractive, with the item list moved to a side panel instead of the main body.

nodes.label: Redesign the report as an interactive dashboard, resolving rendering bugs
nodes.detail: Rebuilds the report as an industrial-style 'Warehouse Manifest' HTML dashboard with stat cards, a stock-value-by-vendor chart, and a searchable sidebar tag list of all items, diagnosing and fixing several rendering issues along the way (a missing-font fallback and a JS compatibility bug that was silently halting the script) before delivering the finished file.

nodes.label: Review the finished warehouse dashboard
nodes.detail: Watches the live dashboard preview render in the split-pane view, checking the stat cards and vendor breakdown before moving on to the next report.

Step 2.step_action: Create a visual report showing each landed container, including items, quantities, and value.

nodes.label: Request an analogous multi-container overview
nodes.detail: Asks Claude for the same kind of visual file but covering sheets 1 through 7, explaining that each sheet represents one landed container.

nodes.label: Reconcile data across all seven container sheets and build a drill-down dashboard
nodes.detail: Extracts and cross-checks each container sheet's structure, headers, and totals (working around inconsistent 'Final' rows and missing shipment dates), verifies computed CBM/volume against the workbook's own totals, and builds a 'Cargo Manifest' dashboard with a cross-container comparison chart plus a switchable per-container detail view and sidebar item list.

nodes.label: Save and briefly review Claude's generated report from previous step
nodes.detail: Downloads Claude's previous HTML report and briefly review it.

nodes.label: Review the container overview dashboard
nodes.detail: Watches the tabbed container dashboard render, checking the landed-value comparison chart and per-container detail before moving to the next report.

nodes.label: Review the excel about the warehosue data used as an input for Claude and compare with Claude's answer

Step 3.step_action: Create a visual report showing containers currently in transit, including items, quantities, and estimated value.

nodes.label: Request an analogous report for the in-transit shipment
nodes.detail: Asks for a similar report about the TRANSIT sheet, explaining it represents a container currently on its way to Omaha.

nodes.label: Restructure the transit data into the shared schema and build a shipment dashboard
nodes.detail: Maps the TRANSIT sheet's line items and cost-composition rows into the same data schema used for the container reports, catches and fixes two string-escaping bugs that were breaking the page's JavaScript, and delivers a 'Transit Shipment Manifest' dashboard with a landed-cost build-up, freight/duty charge breakdown, and an explicit caveat that the figures are pre-customs estimates.

nodes.label: Review the transit shipment dashboard
nodes.detail: Checks the transit dashboard's route status, cost build-up, and sidebar manifest before moving on to the next report.

Step 4.step_action: Create a comprehensive visual report summarizing the next order, including items, quantities, and estimated order value.

nodes.label: Request a comparable overview for the upcoming orders
nodes.detail: Asks for a similar file covering the three planned-order sheets (NEXT 1, NEXT 2, NEXT 3).

nodes.label: Reconcile the order sheets and quantify prospective cost savings
nodes.detail: Verifies each order sheet's item counts, quantities, and totals, computes a current-supplier-cost-versus-landed-cost comparison across all 27 items (a $5,891.48 / 13.9% projected saving), and builds a violet-accented 'Next Orders Overview' dashboard distinguishing its 'planned / not yet ordered' status from the earlier reports, including per-order tabs, vendor breakdowns, and a top-items-by-value table.

nodes.label: Review Claude's generated reports from previous steps
nodes.detail: Review Claude's HTML reports from previous steps

nodes.label: Review the next-orders dashboard generated by Claude
nodes.detail: Checks the Next Orders Overview dashboard's per-order tabs, cost-savings panel, and top-items table before moving on to request the consolidated report.

Step 5.step_action: Create a comprehensive visual report combining all previous reports into a single overview of inventory and logistics activities.

nodes.label: Request a consolidated overview combining the prior reports
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to combine the warehouse, container, and transit dashboards into a single report, explicitly excluding the two order-planning dashboards.

nodes.label: Assemble a unified dashboard with shared navigation
nodes.detail: Merges the three separate dashboards under one top navigation bar into a single 'Supply Chain Overview' file, resolving duplicate-script and DOM ID-collision bugs that arose from combining independently-built HTML documents, then delivers the consolidated report.

nodes.label: Review Claude's generated report about next orders, specifically on order details
Plan the next prompt for Claude by drafting it about visual overview for tariffs and transportation costs
Review and save the consolidated dashboard, specifically checking the container detail section since the volume looks incorrect
nodes.detail: Checks the merged dashboard's navigation between sections, then asks for a new visual overview of how tariff and transportation costs evolved across the seven containers.

nodes.label: Send the previously drafted prompt about a visual overview on tariff and transportation costs
nodes.detail: Asks for a new visual overview of how tariff and transportation costs evolved across the seven containers.

nodes.label: Analyze and chart the cross-container tariff/transportation cost trend
nodes.detail: Reconciles each container's tariff and transportation-cost figures from the workbook and renders an interactive dual-series chart comparing how the two cost components moved across the seven containers, noting they evolved quite differently from one another.

nodes.label: Plan the next prompt for Claude to make sure it has the correct volumes
Check out the excel file about the volume
Check out the Claude's incorrect volumes in the Supply Chain Overview report
Open the delivered reports directly and request a data-accuracy check
nodes.detail: Opens the generated HTML files across several browser tabs to inspect them directly (Warehouse Manifest, Container Shipments, Transit Shipment, Next Orders, Supply Chain Overview) rather than only viewing them in Claude's split-pane preview, then asks Claude to make sure the container volumes are correct.

nodes.label: Audit the volume calculations and correct a real bug
nodes.detail: Investigates the volume/CBM figures across the container data sources, identifies and confirms a genuine calculation bug rather than a false alarm, and patches the corrected volumes into the affected dashboard files before confirming the fix.

nodes.label: Checking out previous Claude's answer about tarriffs and transportation
Draft the next prompt to make an email for his boss abot this report
Review Claude's answer why data inconsistencies happened and compare the numbers with the original data source
Send the previously drafted prompt to Claude that requests a stakeholder summary email
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to write an email to his boss summarizing what's currently in the warehouse and the status of the seven containers.

nodes.label: Synthesize the session's findings into a management summary email
nodes.detail: Composes a concise email draft opening in Outlook, summarizing current warehouse stock, top vendors by value, and the seven landed containers, specifically flagging Container 3 as a cost/volume outlier, and offers to add further detail (e.g. the tariff/freight breakdown) if wanted.

nodes.label: Review the drafted email
nodes.detail: Reads through the composed draft in Outlook, checking the wording and figures, but leaves the recipient field blank and does not send it during this recording.

nodes.label: Add and revise the email draft in Outlook and check out previous reports
Examine Claude's answer again and compare with the real data
Identify and report a data-entry error
nodes.detail: Returns to the reports and points out that the walk-in cold room line in Container 3 should be quantity 1, not the quantity 4 currently shown.

nodes.label: Clarify the correction's financial implication before applying it
nodes.detail: Before changing any numbers, asks whether the line's existing $51,676.75 total reflects a true total price (with only the unit-count label wrong) or should itself drop to the single-unit price, to avoid silently applying the wrong fix.

nodes.label: Confirm the correct total cost
nodes.detail: Clarifies that the total cost should become $12,919.19 for the single unit, confirming the per-unit price was correct and only the quantity was the error.

nodes.label: Recompute and patch the correction across both reports, delivering reconciled totals
nodes.detail: Fixes the walk-in cold room's quantity and cost, recomputes Container 3's and the fleet-wide grand totals, patches the corrected figures into both the Container Shipments Overview and Supply Chain Overview files, and reports the resulting before/after numbers -- also noting the fix incidentally resolves a volume mismatch against the workbook's own note that had been flagged earlier as a data-quality concern.

nodes.label: Checking out Claude's answer that is still wrong figures and decides to end the session because the user needs to be the one who makes the excel clearer.
nodes.detail: Reads the reconciled before/after totals, confirming the fix is complete, then wraps up the session, briefly switching to the Outlook calendar as the recording ends.
